title: Thinking Love Through Abled-Bodiedness: An Impossible Otherness?
content: This essay discusses abled-bodiedness, desire and love, based on self-reflections and insights from previous relationships and literature from disability studies. I discuss socio-historic constructions of abled-bodiedness, highlighting its historical specificity, analytical visibility, and de-naturalisation. By “Otherising” abled-bodiedness, we can contest its ableist mechanisms in our cosmology and society. The narrative in this paper is personal and subjective, based on affective encounters with partners with disabilities and neuro-diversities. I hope to contribute to a better understanding of ableism as a system, its influence and impact on notions of relationship, emotion, and affection.
